pairs.evidence: src/features/home/sub_cockpit/widgets/LinkedDecisionsWidget.tsx:109 The role=alert span only exists inside the Tile error band, which replaces the body at the moment of failure (Tiles.tsx:89), so the region mounts already holding its text and the load failure is silent on most reader/browser pairings; RecentDecisionsWidget.tsx:86 and WalkthroughOfferWidget.tsx:118 repeat the pattern.

techniques.evidence: src/features/home/sub_cockpit/widgets/RecentDecisionsWidget.tsx:86 A per-widget alert region mounts together with its message instead of calling the shell's announce(). The same folder shows the correct shape at WalkthroughOfferWidget.tsx:108 (a persistent role=status mounted empty), so the right shape is already known here.

src/features/home/sub_cockpit/widgets/VerdictWidget.tsx:58 A dangerous option is marked only by a Dot, which renders aria-hidden (Mark.tsx:23). Neither the name nor a description carries the danger, so a screen reader hears it as an ordinary choice.

src/features/home/sub_cockpit/widgets/WalkthroughOfferWidget.tsx:118 The Tile/empty-band primitive does not announce errors, so each widget hand-rolls an alert at the call site, and each one fails the same way.

pairs.subject: accessibility
pairs.evidence: src/hooks/utility/interaction/useRovingTabIndex.ts:11 The one shared roving-tabindex mechanism keys the active member by index, so focus moves to a different item after a resort or filter. A repo-wide grep finds no consumer outside its own file, so every composite hand-rolls its own arrow handling instead.

techniques.evidence: src/hooks/utility/interaction/useRovingTabIndex.ts:28 Index arithmetic, not member identity, so the identity-survives-reuse rule is broken. The hook also has zero consumers.

src/hooks/utility/interaction/useMotion.ts:49 One signal combines the OS query and the in-app data-motion override. Under reduced motion it is an instant settle (REDUCED_MOTION duration 0.01), not a removal, and useMotion.test.ts forces the signal.

src/hooks/utility/interaction/useMenuKeyboard.ts:39 The shared transient-menu model moves focus in on open and hands it back to the trigger on Tab or close (lines 43 and 49-53). Three menus consume it.

pairs.subject: accessibility
pairs.evidence: src/features/shared/components/display/UnifiedTable.tsx:641 Arrow-key row navigation in the shared table stores an index-keyed, visual-only highlight on a scroll container whose outline is removed (:758 focus:outline-none) and that has no aria-activedescendant, so a screen reader hears nothing as the highlight moves and the highlight lands on a different row after a resort.

techniques.evidence: src/features/shared/components/display/UnifiedTable.tsx:758 There is one tab stop with arrows inside it, but position is an index and the container's own focus indicator is removed. The grouped variant at :900/:930 repeats it.
src/features/shared/components/display/UnifiedTable.tsx:344 The loading ghost mounts its own status region already holding the loading label, so most pairings stay silent.
src/features/shared/components/display/SortableHeader.tsx:89 The sort button carries a descriptive name ('Sort by X' or 'Sorted by X'), and aria-sort sits on the columnheader.
src/features/shared/components/display/__tests__/SortableHeader.test.tsx:31 The test queries by role and asserts aria-sort and the computed label, which is what a screen reader receives.
src/features/shared/components/display/ColumnResize.tsx:167 The separator is now keyboard-resizable with aria-valuenow when onNudge is passed, so the earlier pointer-only finding is stale.

src/features/shared/components/display/motionPresets.ts:47 Each preset declares its reduced-motion replacement. MotionizedGlyph.tsx:162 re-detects the OS query ad hoc, but globals.css:5549 still covers the in-app toggle.

pairs.subject: accessibility
pairs.evidence: src/features/shared/components/feedback/AriaLiveProvider.tsx:98 The single provider remounts its live REGION on every message (key changes, at :48-54), so each announcement arrives as a fresh region already holding its text, which most pairings do not voice. The shell's one announcement door is therefore unreliable for every caller.

techniques.evidence: src/features/shared/components/feedback/AriaLiveProvider.tsx:109 The provider and its serial drain (setTimeout at :58) are right, but re-announcing by remounting the region breaks the rule that the region must exist before the news.

src/features/shared/components/feedback/AriaLiveProvider.tsx:28 The re-announce mechanism relies on the pairing-divergent case (a pre-populated new region) instead of a mutation every reader observes.

src/features/shared/components/feedback/Banner.tsx:84 Banner, ErrorBanner (:26) and LoadingSpinner (:15) each own a region that mounts with its content instead of calling the provider, so every consumer inherits the silence.

src/features/shared/components/feedback/ConfirmDialog.tsx:64 isOpen is hard-coded true, so callers close the dialog by unmounting it. BaseModal's focus restore runs only when isOpen flips to false (src/lib/ui/BaseModal.tsx:230-231), so after a confirm or cancel, focus falls back to the document body.
src/features/shared/components/feedback/Banner.tsx:109 The icon-only dismiss button has a translated name.
